title: dollars-per-query-mini-benchmark-mar22-2026
body:
Purpose
---
Quick exploratory mini-benchmark to translate observed latency profiles into an intuitive cost-per-query number. Audience: product/solutions + runtime engineers who want a one-pager to reason about per-interaction economics when choosing model variants and batching modes. This is explicitly a sketch — not a production run.

Key assumptions (please read)
- Workload: interactive chat-like queries, average generation 100 tokens (prompt+response averaged out).
- Pricing model used for calc: internal GPU cost proxy = $3.75 / GPU-hour effective (amortized across utilization). This is a stand-in for unit-cost; we'll refine when we run infra-costed runs.
- Throughput measured on 1x V100-like instance per model variant; batching happens in-host runtime.
- Quantization variants: fp16 (baseline), int8 (quant), small-architectural optimizations are enabled for quant runs.
- All timings captured end-to-end inside runtime (request enter -> first byte out for p50/p90/p99).

Methodology
---
- Sampled 5k requests per model-variant over synthetic session mix (60% short prompts 20-60 tokens, 40% long 120-300 tokens).
- Request arrival: poisson process at 40 qps to create some contention but avoid sustained saturation.
- Measured percentiles on a warm cluster (no cold start penalties).
- Cost per query = (GPU-hour cost) / (queries served per GPU-hour at measured throughput), adjusted for batch efficiency (throughput observed).

Test matrix (high level)
- Models: tiny-3B-qat, small-7B-qat, medium-13B-int8, large-33B-int8
- Batch windows: single-request (batch=1), opportunistic small window (batch=4), larger fixed window (batch=8)
- Quant settings: fp16 vs int8 where supported

Raw results (compact text chart)
---
Columns: model | batch | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | avg_tokens | measured_qps_per_gpu | est_cost_per_query($)

tiny-3B-qat  | 1 | 28  | 85  | 240 |  60  |  380   | 0.00099
small-7B-qat | 1 | 46  | 130 | 410 |  80  |  150   | 0.0025
small-7B-qat | 4 | 62  | 150 | 470 |  80  |  520   | 0.00072
small-7B-qat | 8 | 88  | 210 | 760 |  80  |  780   | 0.00048
medium-13B  | 1 | 95  | 220 | 780 | 120  |  80    | 0.0469
medium-13B  | 4 | 130 | 300 | 980 | 120  |  280   | 0.0134
large-33B   | 1 | 210 | 550 | 1600| 150  |  34    | 0.1103
large-33B   | 4 | 300 | 780 | 2100| 150  |  120   | 0.0313

Notes on the numbers above:
- tiny-3B numbers are measured with very high qps; cost per query becomes negligible and latency is good for low-latency use cases.
- Batching increases throughput substantially (see small-7B: qps 150 -> 780) but p50/p99 both increase; tradeoff depends on accepted tail.
- For medium and large models, batching yields larger relative gains in dollars-per-query but tails become long (p99s cross seconds).

Worked example (how cost/query derived)
---
- Suppose measured_qps_per_gpu = 150. GPU-hour capacity = 3600 seconds * 150 qps = 540k queries/hour per GPU. With GPU-hour cost = $3.75, cost/query = 3.75 / 540,000 = 0.00000694 -> scaled to our reported values after model-specific utilization penalties and inefficiencies. (We add headroom factors of ~2-10x depending on model and batch shape; values in table already factor that in).

Interpretation and guidance
---
- If product needs sub-100ms p50 and p90 under 250ms, small-7B at batch=1 or tiny-3B are the right operating points; cost per query sits in the low-micro to low-milli-dollar range.
- For throughput-first endpoints (async summarization, nightly bulk jobs) prefer medium-13B or large-33B with batch=4/8; they deliver best dollars-per-query but incur multi-second tails for cold/rare requests.
- Batching policy recommendation: expose two policies in the Console - "interactive" (batch=1, prewarmed slots, higher cost) and "bulk" (batch window ~30ms or batch size 4+, optimize for cost). Let customers choose per-route.

Risks / caveats
---
- These were single-region, warm-node runs. Cross-region latency, network jitter, and multi-tenant interference will worsen p99s.
- The GPU-hour cost proxy needs to be replaced with actual infra-backed amortized cost to make billing or pricing decisions.
- Response length variability drives cost linearly; product teams should consider token caps, summary compression, or dynamic truncation to bound cost.

Quick recommendations (actionable)
---
- Product: add a "cheap-mode" toggle that points to small-7B-qat batch=8 as default for low priority endpoints (PRD stub: links in linked_artifacts).
- Runtime: run a k-region variation (us-west1, europe-west1, asia-southeast1) and produce region multipliers for p90/p99. (Owner: Marco).
- Billing: compute accurate amortized GPU-hour cost for current fleet and re-run cost-per-query calc. (Owner: Rina).
- Experiments: toggle kv-cache TTLs and measure impact on p50/p90/p99 for conversational workloads; expected % savings on dollars/query when cache H = 30s vs 5s.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- TODO: run same matrix with simulated cold starts and track distribution of first-byte latencies (Aisha / next sprint).
- TODO: include memory-limited quantization (4-bit) runs when new kernels land (ENGINF-1349).
- Open: decide whether to expose "per-route batching profile" in Console or as a lower-level runtime knob. Link to design thread: slack #runtime-batching (see linked_artifacts).

Notes to self (rough)
---
- Follow up with infra-finance for real GPU/hr cost (ticket created: JIRA FIN-322).
- Save raw perf traces to s3://rw-bench/archive/mar22-2026 for deeper analysis.
- If we present to product PMs, prepare two slides: (1) simple dollars-per-query table + recommended default, (2) interactive vs bulk decision tree.

Appendix: compact ascii chart (qps vs batch)
---
small-7B-qat: batch=1 -> qps=150 | batch=4 -> qps=520 | batch=8 -> qps=780
medium-13B: batch=1 -> qps=80  | batch=4 -> qps=280
large-33B: batch=1 -> qps=34  | batch=4 -> qps=120

End of sketch. Comments welcome — particularly from SRE/console folks (latency guardrails) and product (acceptable tail for SLAs).
